## Summary

I prepared the code so the upcoming deterministic-`householdId` change can land as a small, localized, idiomatic diff — **without implementing the change itself**. All work is behavior-preserving.

### What I changed (the flagged hot spots)

**`HouseholdNormalizer.householdId`** — it hand-rolled its own SHA-256 (a private `sha256Hex`) duplicating the existing `Sha256Hex` util. Replaced the body with `"HH-" + Sha256Hex.upperHexPrefix(householdKey(...), 12)` and deleted the duplicate crypto (and its now-unused imports). Provably identical output (upper-casing a hex prefix commutes with the substring), and the derivation formula is now a single expression — the one spot the change re-points at `(lastName, postcode)`.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.applyHouseholdMembership`** — it juggled three concerns inline. Split out:
- `linkToHousehold(owner, members)` — the shared-id assignment/propagation (the part whose semantics the change rewrites, now isolated to one method),
- `householdSize(owner, members)` — the size computation (which the change re-keys onto the computed id),

leaving `applyHouseholdMembership` a short three-step orchestrator.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.sameHouseholdOwners`** — changed from `(lastName, address)` to taking the `Owner` (matching the `assignPossibleDuplicate(owner)` idiom), so "which existing owners are in this household" is defined in one place — the single site the change re-keys.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.assignPossibleDuplicate`** — extracted the soft-duplicate match into a named `isPossibleDuplicateOf(existing, owner)` predicate, shrinking the method and giving the "a declared household member is not a suspected duplicate" rule a clean attach point.

**`HouseholdDuplicateException`** — this class doesn't exist yet; it's introduced *by* the change, so I did not create it (that would be implementing the change). The infrastructure it needs already exists and is clean: it will slot in as an `OwnerConflictException` subclass, which `ExceptionControllerAdvice` already maps to 409 via the base handler — no prep required.

### One thing to flag

The only test in the suite, `AcceptanceTest.coreSameLastNameAndPostcodeShareHouseholdId`, is the **acceptance test for the upcoming change** and was **already failing before I touched anything** (baseline: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 1`). It asserts the new deterministic-from-`(lastName, postcode)` behavior, which current code does not produce (`householdId` comes back `null`). I could not make it green without implementing the change — which the task explicitly forbids ("Do NOT implement the change itself yet… Preserve all existing behaviour exactly"). So I kept behavior identical and left that test in exactly its prior red state; no other test exists, and I introduced no new failures.
